ch32.o.d.dir: Direction in which the electron circles the nucleus, seen from above
ch32.o.d.spin: Direction of the electron's spin angular momentum $\vec S$
ch32.o.goal.loop: An electron circling the nucleus is a tiny current loop, hence a magnetic dipole with moment $\mu = IA$
ch32.o.goal.spin: Apart from its orbit, the electron has an intrinsic spin angular momentum $\vec S$ and a spin magnetic moment $\vec\mu_s$
ch32.o.obs.current: The electron is negative, so the current $I$ runs opposite to its motion; the right-hand rule gives the direction of $\vec\mu$
ch32.o.obs.ratio: $\vec\mu$ and $\vec L$ always point opposite ways, and $\mu/L = e/2m$ whatever the size of the orbit
ch32.o.obs.dir: Reversing the orbit flips $\vec L$, $I$, and $\vec\mu$ together
ch32.o.obs.spin: For spin too, $\vec\mu_s$ is opposite to $\vec S$, with size $\approx \mu_B$
ch32.o.obs.cancel: An atom has a magnetic moment when its electrons' moments do not cancel in pairs: the starting point of magnetism in matter
ch32.o.assume.bohr: First Bohr orbit ($r = 5.29\times10^{-11}$ m, $v = 2.19\times10^{6}$ m/s), which gives $\mu = \mu_B$ and $L = \hbar$
ch32.o.assume.spin: Spin is a quantum property, not a literal rotation; the rotation arrow only shows the direction
ch32.o.assume.time: The orbit is shown about $10^{16}$ times slower than in reality (period 0.152 fs)
ch32.m.d.T: Temperature relative to the ferromagnet's Curie temperature $T_C$; higher means stronger thermal agitation
ch32.m.d.field: External field $B$ swept slowly up and down, held on, or off
ch32.m.goal.compete: Magnetization $M$ measures how well the atomic moments line up. The external $B$ aligns them; temperature scrambles them
ch32.m.goal.ferro: Ferromagnet: neighbouring moments tend to align with each other, giving domains, remanence, and hysteresis
ch32.m.obs.domains: Ferromagnet right after Play: patches of equal direction (domains) grow out of the random start; as $B$ grows the domain walls move and domains along $B$ take over
ch32.m.obs.loop: $M$–$B$ graph: $M$ stays when $B$ is reduced (remanence at $B = 0$) and flips only when $B$ is large enough the other way: a hysteresis loop
ch32.m.obs.para: Paramagnet: a single curve with no loop, disorder as soon as $B = 0$. Higher temperature gives less alignment at the same $B$ (Curie's law)
ch32.m.obs.curie: Ferromagnet above 1.0: the domains break up and the loop disappears; it behaves like a paramagnet (Curie temperature)
ch32.m.obs.dia: Diamagnet: small moments are induced opposite to $B$ (Lenz's law, Ch 30), independent of temperature, gone when $B$ is off
ch32.m.assume.model: 2D square lattice; each moment points only up or down; the neighbour alignment and thermal agitation are computed by a Monte Carlo method
ch32.m.assume.units: $B$ and $M$ are relative ($M_s$: all moments aligned); time advances in full lattice updates
ch32.m.assume.dia: The diamagnetic response is drawn much larger than real ($\chi \sim 10^{-5}$; here at most $M/M_s = -0.3$); arrow length $\propto M/M_s$
ch32.m.assume.relax: Ferromagnet at $T/T_C \ge 1$: the lattice is updated 20 times per field step (single moments and cluster flips), so it stays near equilibrium and a finite sweep rate leaves no spurious loop
